story.headline: UK inflation jumped to 3.5% in September, above forecasts, making a Bank of England rate hike on November 5 close to certain. Oil climbed back toward $110 as tanker attacks spread to the Gulf of Oman.

reads.policy: Britain's hotter inflation figure makes a Bank of England hike in November close to certain, and an Australian central banker pushed hike bets higher there too. Canada and New Zealand are also expected to raise rates this month, while the Fed holds until December. Currencies whose central banks are about to act keep the rate edge.
reads.growth: Japan's exports grew more slowly than expected, a sign that strong chip demand is not fully offsetting other weakness. US housing remains under pressure from high mortgage rates. Neither changed the rate outlook overnight.
reads.inflation: UK inflation rose more than expected as energy costs fed through, showing the oil shock is still lifting prices. That keeps pressure on central banks to hike rather than wait. Coming up: New Zealand's inflation report at 4:45 PM CT today.
reads.risk: Markets were calm overnight even as tanker attacks reportedly spread into the Gulf of Oman. Hopes for US–Iran diplomacy are holding up without any confirmation, so safe-haven currencies got no fresh lift.
reads.tot: Oil climbed back toward $110 as Gulf shipping risks widened. That helps exporters like Canada and costs importers like Japan, the euro area and Britain, where higher energy bills are already showing up in inflation.
reads.positioning: Hedge funds are betting most heavily against the Canadian dollar, even as a Bank of Canada hike looks likely, which leaves those bets exposed if the loonie keeps rising. They also bet against the kiwi and the euro. In the yen and the Aussie, hedge funds and long-term investors take opposite sides.
reads.fiscal: France's budget fight is on hold until a revenue vote on October 27, with a Moody's review of France on Friday, so the risk to the euro lingers. In Britain, hotter inflation raises the cost of help with energy bills in next week's budget.

fed.summary: The Fed is expected to hold rates on October 28 and raise them in December, because high oil is keeping inflation up. That keeps US rates the highest among the big economies and supports the dollar.
fed.priced: October: hold expected; December: hike very likely.
fed.why: Energy-driven inflation is still too high for the Fed's comfort, even as the housing market weakens under high mortgage rates.
fed.watch: Whether oil stays high enough to keep the December hike alive; the Fed is in its quiet period until the October 28 decision.

boc.summary: The Bank of Canada is widely expected to raise rates on October 28 after warning its inflation forecast will rise sharply on energy costs. That has lifted the loonie to a four-week high.
boc.why: Governor Tiff Macklem said energy will push inflation well above the bank's earlier forecast, outweighing a weak job market.
boc.watch: The October 28 decision and new forecasts; a hold would surprise markets and hit the loonie.

rbnz.summary: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand leans toward a hike on October 28, but tonight's inflation report decides it. A hike would support the kiwi; a hold would hurt it.
rbnz.why: Business activity is strong and dairy prices are firming, but inflation has been cooling and parts of the economy are soft.
rbnz.watch: New Zealand's third-quarter inflation report at 4:45 PM CT today; a figure near forecast keeps the hike on track.

ecb.summary: The ECB is expected to hold on October 29 and lean toward a hike in December, because euro-area inflation is at a three-year high. France's budget trouble is what weighs most on the euro.
ecb.priced: October: hold expected; December: hike likely.
ecb.why: Expensive energy is keeping inflation high, but the ECB wants more evidence before moving again.
ecb.watch: ECB speakers' signals on December, and France's budget vote on October 27 with a Moody's review on Friday.

boj.summary: The Bank of Japan is expected to hold on October 30 and raise rates in December. Higher Japanese rates would narrow the gap with the US and help the yen.
boj.priced: October: hold expected; December: hike likely.
boj.why: Inflation is near the bank's 2% goal and the government says it sees things the same way as the bank, but officials want more proof that wages keep rising.
boj.watch: Japan's inflation figures Thursday evening CT, then the October 29–30 meeting for hints on December.

rba.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia sounds more worried about inflation, and a fifth hike this year is now a real possibility. That has lifted the Aussie to a three-week high.
rba.priced: November: hike possible, about 40%; by March: hike fully expected.
rba.why: Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said the inflation outlook has got materially worse, partly because of high oil.
rba.watch: Australia's third-quarter inflation report on October 28, the deciding number before the November 3 decision.

boe.summary: UK inflation came in hotter than expected, so the Bank of England is almost certain to raise rates on November 5. The debate now is whether it hikes again in December, which supports the pound.
boe.priced: November: hike almost certain; December: second hike debated.
boe.why: Energy costs pushed UK inflation to its highest in 11 months, and pay growth has stopped cooling.
boe.watch: Governor Andrew Bailey's speech at 8:00 AM CT today, the first reaction to the inflation figures.

snb.summary: The Swiss National Bank holds rates at zero and could cut in December, because Swiss inflation is very low. The franc moves more on global worries than on Swiss news.
snb.priced: December: hold or a cut; no hike expected.
snb.why: Swiss inflation is barely above zero and a strong franc keeps import prices down.
snb.watch: The SNB's summary of its September discussion Thursday at 2:30 AM CT, for signs of worry about the franc.

USD.summary: The dollar is near a three-week low as oil and US yields eased, but it still holds the highest rates among the majors with a Fed hike expected in December.

notes.policy: The Fed is expected to hold in October and hike in December, keeping US rates the highest of the majors.
notes.inflation: High oil keeps US inflation well above the Fed's goal, which supports the case for more hikes.

EUR.summary: The euro sits low on the board: a December ECB hike would help, but France's budget fight and the cost of imported energy weigh on it.

notes.policy: The ECB is expected to wait until December, so it trails banks that are hiking sooner.
notes.growth: German investor morale fell and the euro area's trade surplus shrank sharply, both signs of a slowing economy.
notes.inflation: Euro-area inflation is at a three-year high, which keeps a December ECB hike on the table.
notes.tot: Oil near $110 is a heavy bill for the euro area, which imports most of its energy.
notes.fiscal: France's budget fight is unresolved until an October 27 vote, with a Moody's review on Friday.

GBP.summary: The pound is near the top of the board because UK inflation came in hotter than expected and a Bank of England hike on November 5 is almost certain.

notes.policy: A Bank of England hike on November 5 is almost fully expected, and a second in December is being debated.
notes.growth: UK unemployment fell unexpectedly, showing the job market is holding up.
notes.inflation: UK inflation rose to 3.5% in September, above forecasts and far above the Bank of England's 2% target.

JPY.summary: The yen is near the bottom of the board because Japan's rates are far below US rates and high oil makes its imports costly.

notes.policy: The Bank of Japan is expected to wait until December to hike, so the rate gap with the US stays wide.
notes.tot: Japan's oil import bill keeps its trade balance in deficit, a steady drag on the yen.

CHF.summary: The franc is held up by its role as a safe haven, though very low Swiss inflation means the Swiss National Bank could cut rates.

notes.inflation: Swiss inflation is very low, which keeps a December rate cut possible.
notes.risk: Worry about the Gulf and France keeps money flowing into the franc as a safe place to park it.

AUD.summary: The Aussie is near the top of the board because the Reserve Bank of Australia sounds ready to hike again, though a softening job market tempers it.

notes.policy: An RBA official said the inflation outlook has worsened, lifting bets on a November hike.
notes.growth: Australian unemployment is at a five-year high, a sign the economy is cooling.
notes.tot: China's economy grew a little faster than expected, which helps demand for Australian exports.

CAD.summary: The loonie is in the upper half of the board because a Bank of Canada hike on October 28 looks likely and oil prices are high.

notes.policy: Markets expect the Bank of Canada to raise rates on October 28.
notes.growth: Canada lost jobs for a second month in September, a weak spot for the economy.
notes.tot: Oil near $110 boosts Canada's export income.

NZD.summary: The kiwi is supported by a likely Reserve Bank of New Zealand hike on October 28, but tonight's inflation report decides whether that happens.

notes.policy: A Reserve Bank of New Zealand hike on October 28 is likely but depends on tonight's inflation report.
notes.growth: New Zealand factories are expanding at their fastest pace since 2021.
notes.risk: Calm markets and a softer US dollar have helped the kiwi.
notes.tot: Milk powder prices rose at the latest dairy auction, a plus for New Zealand's export income.
